synthesis: Five retrieved records, a small yield, appraised at abstract level. One matched comparison suggests fewer emergency visits after hospital referral to housing first, with engagement as a likely confounder; a methods paper shows how eligible non-referred comparators and a negative control outcome reduce that bias. Hospital referrals are accepted less often than outreach referrals because of incomplete forms and lost contact, and staff describe missing documents and early discharge as the main barriers. People experiencing homelessness will accept data linkage under clear conditions of control and non-disclosure.
gradeRationale: One observational comparison and a programme report for outcomes, with consistent qualitative and methods evidence; confounding by engagement and indirectness to this hospital lower certainty. Low certainty for effects on hospital use; moderate confidence in the referral barriers.
summary: Five retrieved records appraised; five source-derived claims recorded; overall certainty low.
